column1: # The budget of every entry point of the tests and benchmarks (scripts/budget.sh runs under it; scripts/check-budgets.sh fails a runner, a fuzz driver or a stale row without one).
# Tab separated: name, wall seconds, peak tmpfs MB, what and the measurement it rests on. A single run is at most 1800 s (aim 600-1200), an aggregate gate at most 2700 s, tmpfs at most 3072 MB.

column4: what
any test/t file without its own row; the slowest measured 1-seed/-round passes are 400 s (tbl_twin_fuzz) and 900 s only under 4 parallel loops (col_auto_merge_dirty_reads: 152 s alone)

the production viability gate: 27 cases of the four lifecycle classes at 32,768/65,536/131,072 rows in two lanes, the autovacuum_work_mem isolation, the temp_bytes of every case and 3 churns of disk amplification: 45-80 s; tmpfs peak 1,594 MB measured alone (two lane databases of 550-650 MB, each the fixtures of three scales with three wide heap copies, a sift_table and the indexes, plus the autovacuum node)

the load and contention gate: 17 cases of six classes on one cluster; 51-54 s release (F2), 28 s F1 (the Format 2.0 cases skip), 79 s Assert-PG, about 150 s with --determinism; 115-272 MB of tmpfs measured

the workloads suite of the load gate: 28 cases (transactions, online DDL, pooled terminations, tight-memory analytics, projections, tiering, the parallel pool, and the Spec 111, 114, 115 and 116 waves: COPY streams, wide values, tenants under RLS, a BM25 storm, a parallel star join, MERGE and deferred keys, column type changes, concurrent index builds, sketches beside every observability surface, a kill -9 with UNLOGGED objects, 80 savepoints beside lock upgrades, rows moved across sift_table and heap leaves while leaves attach and detach, a scope index under churn and an unprivileged role, connection churn beside the shared memory ledger, prepared transactions through a kill -9) on a cluster of 320 sessions; 72 s release (F2), 43 s F1 and 124 s F2 Assert-PG; 227 MB of tmpfs measured

the stress suite of the load gate: 17 cases of Specs 117 to 119 (serializable write skew through the three engines and projections, cursors held across maintenance, high-cardinality spills under cancels, databases cloned from a template, MERGE and COPY ON_ERROR beside hybrid readers, access method, type and tablespace changes under pg_dump, parts dropped and a table re-keyed under writers, drifting shredded JSONB, connected indexes beside an unprivileged role, VACUUM at the least maintenance_work_mem, 64 pooled sessions under row-level security, BM25 over large documents, sketches and skip indexes under churn, materialized views beside bitmap scans, every row-lock mode across 20 sift_tables, a hybrid as-of join, temporary and unlogged objects through a kill -9) on a cluster of its own; 59 s release with testing (F2), 56 s F1, 57 s release library; 97-143 MB of tmpfs measured

the replication suite of the load gate: a hot standby read, caught up, promoted and cloned again, logical decoding of a sift_table to a subscriber, a standby under recovery conflicts and one promoted while it reads tiered parts and the primary publishes, a REPLICA IDENTITY FULL sift_table and key updates through column changes, VACUUM FULL, CLUSTER and REINDEX CONCURRENTLY replayed under standby readers, a schema of every engine published to a subscriber read while it applies, index-only scans of the standby through VACUUM (FREEZE) and checkpoints; 85-90 s release (F2), 19 s F1, 104 s Assert-PG before the two Spec 118 and 119 cases (60 s of them the liveness cap of the open S115-36 case); 195-322 MB of tmpfs measured (primary, standby and subscriber)
the memory slope gate: 255 s whole (41 cases at 50,000/100,000/200,000 rows, the maintenance cases doing their work in the measured backend), 1.3 GB of tmpfs
